lines.text: Good morning, everyone.
Today, I'll be conducting a short briefing on our AA/SEC/F/077 Attendance Record, specifically on how to properly Check in and Check out using the QR code system.
The purpose of this system is to ensure that every personnel's attendance is recorded accurately, from the beginning of their shift until the completion of their duty.
The process is quite straightforward.
All you need is your mobile phone, your official AirAsia Google account, and the correct QR code.
Throughout this briefing, I'll guide everyone step by step, explain the common mistakes to avoid, and what you should do if you accidentally submit incorrect information.
By the end of this briefing, everyone should be able to complete their attendance independently and correctly.
First, everyone needs to understand that we are using two separate QR codes for attendance.
The first one is the green QR code, which is used for Check-in.
This QR code must be scanned when you start your shift.
The second one is the red QR code, which is used for Check-out.
This QR code must be scanned when you finish your shift.
It's important not to confuse these two QR codes because each one serves a different purpose.
Just remember:
Green means Check-in, at the start of your shift.
Red means Check-out, at the end of your shift.
For both procedures, there are four basic steps:
1. Scan the correct QR code.
2. Complete the required information.
3. Press Submit.
4. Verify that your response has been recorded.
Now, let's go through the Check-in procedure first.

scenes.title: Start of shift: scan the Check-in QR

lines.text: When you report for duty, you must first scan the green Check-in QR code.
Once you scan it, you will be directed to the Google Form.
Before filling in anything, please make sure you are signed in using your official AirAsia Google account.
Do not use your personal Gmail account.
Next, check the title displayed at the top of the form.
The title should be:
AA/SEC/F/077 Attendance Record – Check-in
If the form shows Check-out instead, it means you have scanned the wrong QR code.
In that situation, simply go back and scan the correct green QR code.
Always verify the form title before proceeding.
Once you have opened the correct Check-in form, you will be required to complete several fields.
Let's go through them one by one.
First: Email
At the top of the Google Form, you will see a checkbox to record your email address.
Make sure you tick the Record email checkbox.
This allows your official company email address to be included with your attendance submission.
Second: Designation
You will be asked to select your designation.
There are three options:
Security Executive (DSE)
Security Officer (SO)
Assistant Security Officer (ASO)
Please select your actual designation.
For example, if you are an Assistant Security Officer, select ASO.
Third: Shift Start Date
You must select the date on which your shift begins.
Please make sure you enter the correct date because it will be used to match your Check-in and Check-out records.
Fourth: Name
Enter your name accurately.
Fifth: Staff ID
Enter your correct Staff ID.
This is especially important because your Staff ID is used to identify and match your attendance information.
Please check your Staff ID carefully before submitting the form.
Next, you need to select your assigned team.
As everyone knows, we have four operational teams:
Alpha Team
Bravo Team
Charlie Team
Delta Team
You must select the team you are assigned to for that particular shift.
Now, why is the team selection important?
Because once you submit your attendance, the system will automatically organise the record into the corresponding team's tab in our central Google Sheet.
For example:
Let's say you belong to Bravo Team, but you accidentally select Alpha Team when completing the form.
When you submit your attendance, your record will appear under Alpha Team instead of Bravo Team.
This will result in an incorrect attendance record.
Now, what should you do if this happens?
If you realise that you selected the wrong team before submitting, simply correct your selection.
However, if you have already submitted the attendance form with the wrong team, you must immediately inform your respective Duty Security Executive (DSE).
The respective DSE shall then report the error to the Operations Security Manager for the necessary correction to the attendance record.
Staff must not submit another attendance response to correct the mistake unless instructed by an authorised supervisor.
So, the reporting flow is simple:
Staff → Respective DSE → Operations Security Manager → Attendance Correction
Please remember that attendance corrections must be handled through the proper reporting channel.
Therefore, always double-check your team selection before pressing Submit.

scenes.title: Review, submit and confirm your Check-in

lines.text: Once you have completed the form, don't immediately press Submit.
Take a few seconds to review all the information you have entered.
Make sure:
Your company email is selected.
Your designation is correct.
Your shift start date is correct.
Your assigned team is correct.
Your name is accurate.
Your Staff ID is correct.
After verifying everything, press the Submit button.
You only need to submit your Check-in form once per shift.
Once you press Submit, wait for the confirmation screen.
You should see the message:
"Your response has been recorded."
This confirmation is important because it indicates that your submission has been successfully received.
If you see this message, your Check-in is complete.
However, if the confirmation screen does not appear, check whether there are any missing fields, form errors, or internet connection issues.
If you are unsure whether your attendance has been successfully submitted, inform your supervisor instead of repeatedly submitting the form.
Remember, multiple submissions may create duplicate attendance records.

scenes.title: End of shift: scan the Check-out QR

lines.text: Now, let's move to the Check-out procedure.
Once you have completed your shift, you must record your Check-out.
This time, you must scan the red Check-out QR code.
Please do not scan the green Check-in QR code again.
After scanning, the Google Form will open.
Just like the Check-in procedure, make sure you are using your official AirAsia Google account.
The form title should display:
AA/SEC/F/077 Attendance Record – Check-out
Always check the title before proceeding.
The Check-out procedure is similar to Check-in, but the form is shorter and requires fewer details.
Once the Check-out form opens, you will need to complete the required information.
First, tick the Record email checkbox.
Next, enter your Staff ID.
Please ensure you use the same Staff ID that you entered during Check-in.
After that, select your Shift Start Date.
Now, I want everyone to pay attention to this part, especially those working overnight shifts.
Let's look at one example.
Suppose your shift starts on 11 November at 8:00 PM and finishes on 12 November at 8:00 AM.
When you Check out on 12 November, what date should you select?
The correct answer is 11 November, because that is the date your shift originally started.
You should not select 12 November simply because you are checking out on that date.
The system uses the shift start date to match your attendance correctly.
Next, select the same team used during your correct Check-in.
For example, if you checked in under Bravo Team, your Check-out should also be under Bravo Team.
If you discover that your Check-in contains an incorrect team selection, inform your respective DSE so the error can be reported for correction.
You will notice that the Check-out form does not ask for your name or designation.
This is normal because those details were already provided during Check-in.
Once all required information is completed, press Submit once.
Wait for the confirmation message:
"Your response has been recorded."
Once this appears, your Check-out submission is complete.
Now, there is one important feature I want everyone to understand.
You do not need to manually enter your Check-in or Check-out time.
The system automatically records the timestamp when you submit the Google Form.
For example, let's say your shift starts at 8:00 AM.
If you submit your Check-in form at 8:05 AM, the system will record the submission timestamp as 8:05 AM.
Similarly, if you complete your shift and submit your Check-out at 8:10 PM, the system will record the submission timestamp as 8:10 PM.
You don't need to type any time manually.
In fact, the forms do not provide a field for you to enter your own time.
The timestamp is automatically captured and reflected in the attendance Google Sheet.
Therefore, please make sure you submit your Check-in when reporting for duty and your Check-out when completing your shift.
Remember:
No manual time entry is required.

scenes.title: Where does your attendance record go?

lines.text: Now, some of you might be wondering what happens after you submit the form.
Let me explain.
Once you press Submit, your attendance response is automatically recorded in our central Google Sheet.
The system organises the information according to the team you selected.
For example:
If you select Alpha Team, your attendance will appear in the Alpha tab.
If you select Bravo Team, your attendance will appear in the Bravo tab.
The same applies to Charlie and Delta.
The Google Sheet contains your attendance information, including the recorded Check-in and Check-out timestamps.
These records can be monitored and reviewed by authorised supervisors.
As staff, you do not need to access or manually update the Google Sheet.
Your responsibility is to use the correct QR codes, complete the forms accurately, and verify that each submission is successful.
Before we finish, I want to highlight a few common mistakes that everyone should avoid.
Mistake 1: Scanning the wrong QR code
Some staff may accidentally scan the Check-out QR code when starting duty.
Always remember:
Green for Check-in and red for Check-out.
Mistake 2: Selecting the wrong team
Always verify that you have selected your assigned team.
If you accidentally submit attendance under the wrong team, immediately inform your respective DSE.
The DSE shall report the issue to the Operations Security Manager for correction.
Do not submit another form to try to fix the error yourself unless authorised.
Mistake 3: Entering the wrong Shift Start Date
This is particularly important for overnight shifts.
Remember that the shift start date must remain the same during both Check-in and Check-out.
Mistake 4: Using a personal Gmail account
Always use your official AirAsia Google account when completing both forms.
Mistake 5: Submitting multiple responses
You only need one successful Check-in and one successful Check-out for each shift.
If you have received the confirmation message, do not submit another response.
Mistake 6: Forgetting to Check out
Some personnel may complete their Check-in but forget to submit their Check-out.
This will result in an incomplete attendance record.
Therefore, before leaving duty, always ensure that your Check-out has been properly submitted.
If you encounter any issues or realise that you have submitted incorrect information, inform your respective DSE so the matter can be reported through the proper channel.
Alright, everyone. Before we end today's briefing, let's quickly recap the whole procedure.
At the beginning of your shift:
Scan the green Check-in QR code.
Sign in using your official AirAsia Google account.
Complete all the required information, including your designation, shift start date, team, name, and Staff ID.
Review your details, press Submit once, and verify that your response has been recorded.
At the end of your shift:
Scan the red Check-out QR code.
Use the same official AirAsia Google account.
Enter the same Staff ID and shift start date, and select your correct team.
Press Submit once and wait for the confirmation message.
Now, there are three important rules I want everyone to remember:
Rule 1: Always use your official AirAsia Google account.
Rule 2: Never enter or change the attendance time manually. The system records it automatically.
Rule 3: Submit each form only once per shift and always verify the confirmation message.
And one additional reminder:
If you accidentally submit incorrect attendance information, immediately report it to your respective DSE.
The DSE shall escalate the matter to the Operations Security Manager for the necessary correction.
The purpose of this procedure is to ensure that our attendance records remain accurate, properly organised, and available for authorised supervisory review.
Everyone is responsible for ensuring that their attendance is recorded correctly.
That concludes the briefing on the AA/SEC/F/077 Attendance Record.
Thank you, everyone, for your attention and cooperation.
Before we finish, does anyone have any questions regarding the Check-in or Check-out procedure?
Staff understanding check.
Which QR code should you scan at the beginning of your shift?
The green Check-in QR code.
Which QR code should you scan after completing your shift?
The red Check-out QR code.
Can you use your personal Gmail account?
No. Only the official AirAsia Google account should be used.
If your shift starts on 11 November at 8:00 PM and ends on 12 November at 8:00 AM, which date should you select during Check-out?
11 November, because that is the shift start date.
If you accidentally select Alpha Team instead of Bravo Team and have already submitted the form, what should you do?
Immediately inform the respective DSE. The DSE shall report the error to the Operations Security Manager for the necessary attendance correction.
Do you need to manually enter your Check-in and Check-out times?
No. The system automatically records the time of submission.
How do you confirm your attendance was successfully submitted?
The Google Form displays "Your response has been recorded."
Can you submit the same Check-in form multiple times?
No. Only one successful Check-in submission is required per shift.
Who can review the attendance records in the central Google Sheet?
Authorised supervisors.
What must you do before completing your duty?
Scan the red Check-out QR code, complete the form, submit it, and verify the confirmation.
End of training. AA/SEC/F/077 – Attendance Record Staff Guidance
